audit.whatIsWrong: The reflect is attributed to Mel's ULT in three places — spikes[2].when literally reads 'Her R active' and the text says 'while Mel's R is up — her reflect bounces your magic burst back'. The reflect is Rebuttal, her W. Her R is Golden Eclipse.
audit.why: A player counting a 120-second ultimate cooldown while the real barrier is a 38-to-26 second W will step into it two or three times per lane phase. The two abilities also want opposite responses: you wait Rebuttal out, but you cannot wait out a global execute.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].when set to 'Her W active' and the text, content.late, wants.foe[1], tradeBad, breakdown.cooldowns and Key Ability Interactions all name Rebuttal.

audit.whatIsWrong: Golden Eclipse is absent from both layers. It strikes every enemy carrying Overwhelm regardless of distance — a 25000-unit range, which is the whole map.
audit.why: The page's entire escape plan is 'blink out'. Against a global execute keyed to a stacking debuff, distance is not safety: a Kassadin who disengages at 30% carrying Overwhelm stacks dies in the fountain lane. This is the missing-interactions file's execute-threshold entry and it never reached the page.
audit.corrected: Added to wants.foe[2], content.late, phases[6].why and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rebuttal is treated as blanket protection from Kassadin's burst. It has two distinct effects and only one of them is symmetric: it prevents Mel from taking damage at all, but it only REFLECTS projectiles.
audit.why: Null Sphere is a targeted projectile and comes back at you. Riftwalk's arrival damage and Force Pulse's cone are not projectiles — they still do nothing to her, but they do not rebound. That is the difference between a wasted rotation and a suicide.
audit.corrected: Split out in spikes[2].text and tradeBad — nothing damages her through it, only the Q punishes you for trying.

audit.whatIsWrong: Solar Snare's root is treated as a lockout Riftwalk has to avoid. Riftwalk is a blink, and roots do not disable blinks.
audit.why: Her E is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s on a 1000-range projectile and it is her only way to hold Kassadin still. If the root does not hold the blink, the ability stops being the reason he cannot commit — and the page currently builds the whole level-6 section on the assumption that it does.
audit.corrected: Stated in spikes[1].text, whys[4], phases[4].why, content.mid, breakdown.mid and Key Ability Interactions.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns says 'Count it out loud if you must' and gives no number for anything.
audit.why: Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26s — by far the longest lane cooldown either champion has, and the single thing that decides when Kassadin can commit. Solar Snare is 11s to 9 and Radiant Volley 10s to 6.
audit.corrected: All three written into breakdown.cooldowns, tradeGood, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, phases[3].why and All-In Windows.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0] to [6] are the generic Kassadin boilerplate and none of them names a Mel ability. The packet flags this matchup for naming none of Searing Brilliance, Radiant Volley, Rebuttal, Solar Snare or Golden Eclipse anywhere.
audit.why: The spikes in this lane are hers and they are specific: a 950-to-650 range gap early, Rebuttal's long cooldown mid, and a global execute late. 'You are the worst champion in the game for ten minutes' describes none of it.
audit.corrected: phases[0], [2], [3], [4], [6] and breakdown.early/mid rewritten around the real abilities and ranges.

audit.whatIsWrong: content win[] reads Mel/Mel/Mel/Mel/Skill/Skill/Kassadin. The packet's levelChart and the existing mirror audit both give Mel/Mel/Skill/Skill/Kassadin/Kassadin/Kassadin.
audit.why: The two directions of the same matchup currently disagree at four of seven stages, and my page is the one out of step with the packet.

audit.whatIsWrong: Void Stone is stated as '15% magic reduction' in spikes[3], wants.you[2], content.early and whys[3]; phases[2].why carries the 'E only charges when spells fly' boilerplate.
audit.why: Void Stone has been 10% since V11.24 and Force Pulse stopped being charge-gated in V12.23 — it is now a 21/20/19/18/17s cooldown shortened by one second per nearby ability cast.
audit.corrected: 15% set to 10% in all four places; phases[2].why rewritten to the cooldown model.

edits.before: Mel out-ranges you hard for the first three levels — her Q pokes you down while your Null Sphere is point-blank and your mana pool is empty, so don't walk up trying to land a Q she can simply sidestep. Last-hit at max range, accept a little chip, and look to put a point in W early so Nether Blade's mana restore off the wave keeps you online and unpushable. Your one cushion is Void Stone: her AP poke is cut 15% before it even lands, so she whittles you down slower than she would any other melee.
edits.after: Mel out-ranges you hard for the first three levels — Radiant Volley reaches 950 while your Null Sphere reaches 650, and your mana pool is empty, so don't walk up trying to land a Q she can simply sidestep. Last-hit at max range, accept a little chip, and put a point in W early so Nether Blade's mana restore keeps you online and unpushable. Your one cushion is Void Stone: her poke is cut 10% before it lands, so she whittles you down slower than she would any other melee.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still a weather-the-storm window — keep Q maxed and pop the Null Sphere shield to eat her incoming Q so the poke does almost nothing, and farm under tower if she shoves. At 6 the lane equalizes: Riftwalk lets you blink through her W/E zone or straight onto her if she over-extends, and the shield plus Void Stone reduction mean a poke war now favors your sustain. Bait her to step up for a Q, blink in, and force the short trade her squishy frame loses — just hold the blink until her R isn't up.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are still a weather-the-storm window — keep Q maxed and pop the Null Sphere shield to eat Radiant Volley so the poke does almost nothing, and farm under tower if she shoves. At 6 the lane equalizes: Riftwalk blinks through Solar Snare, because roots do not stop blinks, or straight onto her if she over-extends, and the shield plus Void Stone mean a poke war now favors your sustain. Bait her step-up, blink in, force the short trade her frame loses — never into Rebuttal.

edits.before: Once Rod of Ages is online and Riftwalk is maxed, you flip the script — your blink-spam mobility, Q shield, and Void Stone reduction make you the textbook anti-mage who eats her entire damage profile. The single thing that punishes you here is Mel's R: do NOT blink in and unload Riftwalk + Q while her reflect is active, because it bounces your magic straight back. Track that cooldown, blink the instant it's down, and her lack of an escape means a stacked Riftwalk runs her out of options.
edits.after: Once Rod of Ages is online and Riftwalk is maxed you flip the script — blink-spam, the Q shield and Void Stone make you the textbook anti-mage who eats her damage profile. Two things still punish you. Rebuttal reflects projectiles, so never dump Null Sphere into it: 38s at rank 1, down to 26. And Golden Eclipse strikes every enemy carrying Overwhelm regardless of distance, so walking out of lane does not walk you out of its range. Track both, then blink in.

notes: MIRROR: audits/top/mel__kassadin.json exists and I reused its findings rather than re-deriving them — Null Sphere interrupts channels rather than being one, Void Stone plus the Null Sphere shield as two separate magic layers, and Riftwalk at 5/3.5/2s. My side states the same facts inverted. BLOCKED BY THE LENGTH BAND, AND IT IS A MIRROR CONFLICT: my content win[] reads Mel/Mel/Mel/Mel/Skill/Skill/Kassadin, while the packet's levelChart and the mirror audit both record Mel/Mel/Skill/Skill/Kassadin/Kassadin/Kassadin. Four of seven stages disagree across the two directions of the same matchup. 'Mel' to 'Skill' is 3 chars to 5 (+67%) and 'Skill' to 'Kassadin' is 5 to 8 (+60%) — every one of the four blows the band, in both content win[] and full phases[].side. This needs a hand fix or mirror-fix.js will have to arbitrate. THE MIRROR ALSO CARRIES ONE STALE MECHANIC I did not copy: it says 'casting near Kassadin charges Force Pulse'. Force Pulse has not been charge-gated since V12.23 — nearby casts reduce its cooldown by a second each instead. The effect is similar in practice but the wording should be brought in line. CHAMPION-WIDE: Void Stone is 10%, not 15% (V11.24), and the 'E only charges when spells fly' phases[2] boilerplate is on all 71 Kassadin matchups.
